question: Why did Nightingale-style wards have tall windows facing each other along both long walls?
answer: To sweep out foul air, because Nightingale held that disease rose from miasma, not germs. Her Notes on Hospitals demanded long, narrow pavilions with windows on opposite walls and open space between buildings. The theory was wrong, but the cross-draught diluted real airborne germs, and one nurse at the end could see every bed.
move: A wrong theory can still build the right room.
ask: What good result of mine came from a wrong theory I should now stop crediting?
reference: McDonald (ed.), Florence Nightingale and Hospital Reform, Collected Works of Florence Nightingale vol. 16, Wilfrid Laurier University Press, 2012
